paragraphs.text: Systolic blood pressure was assessed using a noninvasive tail-cuff system (IITC Life Science Inc.) for model-success screening at baseline and on days 7, 14, 21, and 28 after model induction. The chamber was set to 30°C, prewarmed for 10 min, and checked for cuff sealing. Rats were placed in the restrainer with the tail passing through the cuff and allowed to rest for 15 min. BPmon Win monitor 1.35 was used for acquisition; the value at the onset of the spindle-shaped waveform was recorded as systolic blood pressure. Three measurements were averaged for each rat. Blood-pressure observations from the source experiment were shared with the related report [22]. Archived worksheet rows and entered restoration summaries are additionally provided in S2 Fig, S3 and S4 Data, and S5 File. Original block labels and source cells were retained, without selecting animals by their pressure values or reconstructing the terminal three-group cohorts. Row counts were not treated as verified independent animal counts or used for a new blood-pressure treatment-effect test.

Codex (OpenAI) assisted with language editing, methodological review, worksheet checking, statistical reanalysis, and development of analysis and plotting code. Figs 1 and 2 and S2 Fig were produced from numerical records using conventional plotting code. S1 Fig reused the previously formatted source composite, with English group labels outside the images and preserved tissue and original scale-bar pixels. No experimental images or original experimental data were generated by these tools. The authors manually checked the biochemical and qPCR numerical results, figures, and conclusions and retain responsibility for the accuracy and final verification of the manuscript and supplementary material.

The archived workbook retained 24, 14, and 10 identifier rows under model, control, and sham-operation headers, respectively, from the preoperative time point through week 4; the recorded values are displayed in S2 Fig. Recalculated means and sample SDs for the 10 complete sham-labelled rows at all five time points matched the sham summaries in the first part of the source thesis. Missing observations and repeated labels in the model and separately labelled control blocks prevented unique identification of the 10 animals in the current model group. Only four entered restoration summaries were available for weeks 5–8, without corresponding animal-level distributions or dispersion estimates. These stored rows and summaries were therefore not used for a terminal three-group blood-pressure comparison or an independent model validation. The complete original workbook is retained in S5 File.

S2 Fig. Descriptive display of blood-pressure records in the source workbook. Panels A–C show the preoperative-to-week-4 blocks originally labelled model, control, and sham operation, retaining 24, 14, and 10 source rows, respectively. These row counts are not verified independent animal sample sizes. Each point represents a stored numeric cell; lines connect only consecutive non-missing time points within the same source row. Repeated labels are not merged, and missing observations interrupt lines. Panel D shows four entered restoration summaries at weeks 5–8; corresponding effective animal counts and dispersion estimates were unavailable. The original control label was retained without reassignment to sham or restoration. No error bars, P values, confidence intervals, or inferential statistics are shown, and the records do not establish a terminal three-group blood-pressure treatment comparison. Cell-level inputs, entered summaries, and the complete workbook are provided in S3 Data, S4 Data, and S5 File, respectively. Codex (OpenAI) assisted in developing the plotting code.

S3 Data. All 240 value positions in the three archived blood-pressure record blocks, including missing cells, original headers and identifiers, source rows and columns, and keys locating source rows. Record keys do not replace animal identities or establish terminal-group assignment or pairing across assays.

S4 Data. Original entered summaries under the model, sham-operation, and restoration labels in the archived workbook, including missing positions. Source labels are retained without treating them as verified allocations; the original sham-labelled summaries correspond numerically to the separately labelled control block. Animal counts and dispersion estimates were not imputed.

S5 File. Unmodified original blood-pressure workbook, retaining source records, labels, and embedded charts. S2 Fig displays the source records without adopting the inconsistent group attribution in the original embedded charts.
S3 Appendix. Conventional plotting script reproducing S2 Fig from S3 and S4 Data. It displays the source records without animal-identity reconstruction, outlier exclusion, or inferential statistics.
